key_insight: Data-driven equation discovery can recover liquid-film flow dynamics in a best-case setting, but multicollinearity and early-time transients make the governing equations hard to identify reliably.
engineering_relevance: The work clarifies where equation-discovery methods can help model complex thin-film flows and where they may fail, informing more robust reduced-order and physics-informed modeling pipelines.
method: Curated liquid-film flow data with expert-selected candidate terms
Used monomial basis functions to discover governing PDE structure
Analyzed identifiability under multi-scale dynamics and transient-rich regimes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that even with carefully curated data and expert knowledge, multicollinearity and transient-dominated residuals exposed identifiability limits in the training data.
watch_item: Monomial basis choices and early-time transient data can bias discovery, so implementation should guard against multicollinearity and unstable coefficient recovery.
paper_title: Data-Driven Equation Discovery for Nonlinear Liquid Film Flows
